item.title: Brazil heads to the polls for high-stakes election between Lula and Flavio Bolsonaro
item.description:
This article is a partnership with Agência Pública . In May, now-presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro, the eldest son of former Brazilian far-right President Jair Bolsonaro, shared on his social media a “ leaked ” trailer for an upcoming biopic about his father. The “most anticipated movie of the year,” Flávio said then, would depict the story of a “true hero.” In the trailer, which had a “disclosure prohibited” watermark, a wig-wearing Jim Caviezel — the American Hollywood actor perhaps most famous for his role as Jesus in Mel Gibson’s 2004 The Passion of the Christ — plays Bolsonaro, who is serving a 27-year prison sentence under house arrest for a failed coup attempt after his 2022 electoral defeat. item.title: Russia strikes Kyiv bridge as German chancellor visits Ukraine in show of support
item.description:
Attack shortly after Friedrich Merz arrived on unannounced visit intended to underline Germany’s backing Russia has struck another major bridge in Kyiv as the German chancellor, Friedrich Merz, arrived in the capital in a show of support for Ukraine. A Russian drone hit Kyiv’s key Northern Bridge over the Dnipro River, marking the fourth consecutive day that Russia has targeted bridges used by tens of thousands of residents commuting between the city’s two banks. Video footage showed cars driving across the bridge as the drone plunged into the roadway and exploded in a burst of fire. Two people were injured in the strike, said Kyiv’s mayor, Vitali Klitschko. item.title: Accidental Environmentalist? How Trump’s War Exposed the Fragility of Dirty Energy.
item.description:
This story was originally published by The Guardian and is reproduced here as part of the Climate Desk collaboration. Of all the epithets hurled at Donald Trump since he became US president, perhaps the most unusual was delivered last month—that he is, in fact, some sort of environmentalist. Trump is the “greatest gift” to the environmental movement, argued Gavin Newsom, California’s governor, due to the fallout from the US-Israel war on Iran . “He’s woken the world up to how vulnerable we are to petro-dictatorships, how vulnerable we are to disruptions in the Middle East,” Newsom told The Guardian during Climate Week in New York. “This war has completely gutted any sort of romantic notions of energy security and it’s compelled folks to think differently. item.title: Brazilians vote for next president as Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro hope for first round victory
item.description:
Brazil votes Sunday in a presidential election that could reshape its relationship with President Trump , return the Bolsonaro movement to power and alter the future of the Amazon. Why it matters: The showdown between President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro has turned into something bigger: a test of Trump's influence in Latin America's largest country, with stakes for the region and the global climate. The latest: Trump said Thursday he's following Brazil's election "very closely" and called it "very important," though he didn't endorse a candidate. Catch up quick: Trump inserted the U.S. into the contest when his administration imposed additional 25% tariffs on some Brazilian goods this summer — prompting Lula to accuse the American leader of "interference" in Brazil's affairs. item.title: How was Flydubai co-pilot cleared despite being deemed a security risk?
item.description:
Oman had banned the FlyDubai co-pilot accused of stabbing his captain in an attempted hijacking from flying over concerns that he had adopted “radical ideological views,” according to a new report. Despite the ban, FlyDubai hired the Omani national, allowing him to fly the route between the United Arab Emirates and Israel, The Wall Street Journal reported. The Journal could not determine whether Oman had shared its concerns about the suspected terrorist with other airlines or countries Aviation-security analysts told The Journal that the attack exposed a major security failure. Even if a screening lapse allowed a weapon through, they said, a motivated assailant should have been stopped before reaching the airport. item.title: Would a Firing Squad Have Been More 'Humane' for Christa Pike?
item.description:
Christa Pike, the Tennessee woman convicted of murdering Colleen Slemmer in 1995 , was a dead woman walking Wednesday. Whether or when she will walk again remains to be seen. But, as of Thursday evening, she was alive, having survived the state's attempt to execute her via lethal injection. Twice. Put differently, it did not go as planned. Correctional staff administered a (supposedly) lethal dose of pentobarbital, a barbiturate, around 7:30 p.m. "My arm feels like it's about to burst open," Pike said, according to a reporter who was there to witness the execution. Pike thrashed and did not die. So staff closed the death-chamber curtain and administered another dose, after which she began loudly snoring and struggling for air. Pike was subsequently transferred to a hospital, where she was intubated and put on a ventilator as medical personnel worked "to save [her] life," her attorneys…

item.title: ‘Did he know?’: Why Israel is rejecting an October 7 reckoning
item.description:
An Israeli strike on a civilian vehicle in Gaza on Sunday killed one Palestinian and wounded at least 11 others. Israel’s military said it was targeting a Hamas militant. Palestinians have reported a surge in Israeli fire and airstrikes across Gaza over the past month, with more than 75,000 people killed and much of the enclave destroyed. Meanwhile, Israelis held their weekly protest in Tel Aviv’s Hostages Square, the last before Wednesday marks three years since the October 7 attack. Protesters said they wanted to commemorate the victims and demand an independent state inquiry into the events and decisions that led to the attack. The Hamas-led assault killed around 1,200 people in Israel and saw more than 250 others taken hostage, according to Israeli authorities. Rachael Goldberg Polin, an American-Israeli activist and mother of slain hostage Hersh Goldberg-Polin, speaks to France 24.

Covered by 2 public.
Sources: Al Jazeera English, France 24

item.title: Medicare for All remains key pressure point for Democrats ahead of midterms
item.description:
The idea of universal health coverage in the US is embraced by party’s left but is often considered a liability by centrists Last week, 1,500 unionized nurses gathered in a large conference room at the Marriott Marquis in San Francisco to cheer for a cause they’ve championed for years: Medicare for All. Considered a radical and even fringe idea for decades, interest in sweeping healthcare reform has surged as progressive Democrats have won a series of primary victories ahead of November’s crucial midterm elections. Most prominent among its advocates is Democratic US Senate nominee from Michigan Abdul El-Sayed – who took the lectern before these nurses. Continue reading...
